name: Arizona
agency: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division (ADOT MVD)
permitAge: 15 years and 6 months (Class G instruction permit, under 18)

teen.supervisedHours: 30 hours, including 10 at night (or completion of an MVD-approved driver education program; one source says 20 hours with 6 at night after an approved school)
teen.holdPermit: 6 months (third-party sources; not confirmed on azdot.gov)
teen.nightLimit: First 6 months of the graduated (Class G) license: no driving midnight to 5 a.m. unless a licensed parent or guardian is in the front passenger seat; secondary sources list exemptions for work, school, religious activities and family emergencies
teen.passengerLimit: First 6 months: no more than one passenger under 18, except siblings or when a parent/guardian is in the front seat (GHSA and iDriveSafely; not confirmed on azdot.gov)
teen.phone: Instruction permit holders may not use a wireless communication device while driving except in an emergency (Laws 2017, ch. 209; ARS 28-3154). All drivers: hands-free mode only (ARS 28-914, DPS).

notes: Knowledge test stops automatically once 80 percent are correct or the maximum misses are reached; retake on the next business day (ADOT).
Permit supervisor must sit beside the permittee; current secondary sources say the supervisor must be 21 or older.
Move over law (ARS 28-775): applies to any stationary vehicle with flashing lights since 2011; move to a non-adjacent lane if safe, otherwise slow down.

Prima facie speeds (ARS 28-701): 15 mph approaching a school crossing, 25 mph in business or residential districts, 65 mph elsewhere. Rural interstate 75 mph only where ADOT orders it (ARS 28-702.04); not used as a question.
Extreme DUI at 0.15 BAC or more.
8 or more points in 12 months: Traffic Survival School or suspension (ADOT). TSS is required after DUI, wrong-way, red-light or stop-sign, or aggressive driving convictions.
Minimum liability insurance 25/50/15 since July 1, 2020 (secondary sources).
School bus rule on divided highways: Arizona statute text (ARS 28-857) could not be retrieved; no question written.

Official manual PDF URL could not be confirmed: azdot.gov and azleg.gov were unreachable from this environment and search returned only mirror copies. Secondary sources say an official Spanish manual exists.
Spanish knowledge test: secondary sources say English and Spanish at most offices; not confirmed on azdot.gov.
